messages:
ryan_sales: Acme POC blocked — getting 401s in their integration tests and security team wants IP restriction options. Can we triage?
acme_dev: Yep, all our integration calls return 401 Invalid API key. We copied the key from the onboarding email into env var RWD_KEY. No extra headers set.
dev_jordan: Quick sanity: are you using the hosted endpoint `https://api.redwood.inference/v1/` and `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>`? Also what does the key prefix look like?
acme_dev: Using the hosted endpoint and Authorization header. Key starts `rwd-` (looks like production).
infra_bot: secrets: looked up fingerprint for key used in request id rwd-req-9f4c2. status: disabled by rotation, bound_org: org-22, bound_project: web-demo.
acme_dev: Wait it's disabled? We didn't rotate it. We saw logs earlier showing it active.
security_sam: Two possibilities: key was manually rotated or there was an automated rotation policy for old PoC keys. Also check if your service is sending an `X-RWD-Org-Id` or `X-RWD-Project-Id` that doesn't match binding. Mismatched org/project can also surface as 401/403 depending on policy.
acme_dev: We're not setting any org/project headers explicitly — using the Go SDK default.
dev_jordan: The SDK will attach org/project from env if set. Can you paste env dump (sanitized)?
acme_dev: `RWD_KEY=rwd_abc123
RWD_ORG=org-labs
RWD_PROJECT=demo`
dev_jordan: That shows it — your env org is org-labs but key bound to org-22. If the SDK sends RWD_ORG it overrides token binding and server rejects.
acme_dev: Ohhh. That env var came from earlier internal tests. We restarted with the right env and still 401.
infra_bot: secrets: current key rwd_abc123 status: disabled. Last action: `rotate` at 2026-01-12T03:14:22Z. Bound_org: org-22.
acme_dev: So the key was rotated/disabled. Can you issue a short-lived key for our PoC org org-acme? We need to unblock tests.
ryan_sales: We can. @infra_bot or @dev_jordan can create a scoped PoC key (inference-only) and note expiry. Also Acme asked about IP allowlist for security questionnaire.
dev_jordan: For hosted PoCs we support scoped keys (inference-only, embeddings-only) and short expiry. IP allowlisting is available for enterprise Dedicated/Private tenants only. We can note that in the security response.
infra_bot: secrets: created key `rwd-test_acme_temp_21` bound_org: org-acme, bound_project: poc, scopes: [inference:generate], expires: 48h, status: active. id: rwd-test_acme_temp_21.
acme_dev: Swapped to new key and re-ran tests — now seeing 200s. Thank you.
security_sam: I'll draft the security answer: "Hosted keys can be scoped and time-limited for PoCs. IP/CIDR allowlist and HSM-backed keys available on Dedicated/Private deployments."
ryan_sales: FYI: customer also reported transient 429s when run parallel embedding jobs. Any recommended limits for initial ramp?
dev_jordan: For PoC accounts we recommend conservative defaults: start at 50 req/min per client, use token streaming to reduce burst, batch embeddings into chunks of 8-16 items, add exponential backoff with full jitter on 429s. Monitor `x-rwd-remaining` header.
acme_dev: Do you have a sample backoff snippet for JS?
dev_jordan: Sending DM with snippet. Also opening a small UX ticket: console should show key binding (org/project) and last rotation timestamp next to keys.
ryan_sales: Please attach the new key id to the PoC record and include the rate guidance in the PoC runbook.
infra_bot: crm: PoC ACME-POC-88 updated with key rwd-test_acme_temp_21 and notes.
acme_dev: All good now, appreciate the fast help. Closing this thread unless something else pops. :white_check_mark:
